passages.notes: Full UTF8 body including final LF SHA256 c767db70fa4486fbeedb5a3dba2e9a15c5313133a4ef671d361fc0c4439db840. Mame 1922 whole PDF 839/printed 725 supplies the complete named petition and actual Per Dominum. stop. Target1962 whole PDF 749/printed 668/no3714 prints natalicia and actually stops at Per Dominum nostrum. Source natalitia and target natalicia are the same substantive neuter accusative plural direct object of colimus, an explicitly declared received noun spelling. Separately registered Pustet 1862 whole PDF 390/printed 304 Praesta prints Per Dominum nostrum contiguously; only this three-word prefix supports the target actual longer cue, with no added tail. Pustet is formula evidence, not the historical Cosmas petition witness. Current wraps, final LF and all Latin body bytes remain unchanged.

work.description: A project-created editorial source projection containing bounded Latin prayer bodies in date-specific artifacts. It is neither an edition of a historical hand missal nor an edition of the Missale Romanum. Each artifact records the transformation rule over separate public-domain antecedent and 1962 page-image witnesses; its passages let consumers cite the projected bodies without assigning Triptych's target-controlled collation choices to the antecedent printing.
